title: Close definition-layer gaps in the model rather than a remainder overlay
decision_statement: Metamodel v1.1.0 must express the live definition-layer surface in SRS records and emit the complete artifact; it must not depend on a hand-maintained remainder overlay for meaning the records cannot carry.

sources.excerpt: Owner confirms 'do not build the remainder overlay': requiring a side-channel for the model's own meaning would undermine portable, self-contained documents and produce non-interoperable community side-channels.
The outcome says to close the generated-subset-of-seed gap by modelling the live post-242 surface and explicitly forbids a hand-maintained remainder overlay.

alternatives: Keep the core metamodel smaller and merge a hand-maintained remainder/*.json overlay into generated schemas.
accepted_cost: The metamodel and emitters must become expressive enough to carry the full live definition layer, increasing modelling and projection work.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: A smaller metamodel and easier emitter would leave part of SRS meaning in repository-specific infrastructure.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Generated schemas and reader-facing projections remain practical outputs of the records.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Adding model machinery solely to reproduce incidental schema syntax rather than semantic meaning would over-rotate.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Keep the v1.0.0 metamodel boundary and preserve its known fidelity exclusions through an overlay.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The frozen bootstrap seed remains the runtime fixed point under RFC-033.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Changing the bootstrap contract while closing build-time authorship gaps would exceed this decision.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Each community could maintain an external side-channel for facets its records cannot express, at the cost of interoperability.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Communities retain their own records and extension packages; coherence is achieved through the portable model, not a central service.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: A common model that prevents communities from defining sanctioned extensions would defeat the stated sovereignty goal.

coding_notes: Owner-ratified design rule. This is distinct from A06's initial self-hosting precedent: it decides how to close the remaining definition-layer gap.

title: Self-host definition extensions as inherited extension Types
decision_statement: Lifecycle, inheritance, validation, identity, and other extension-contributed definition facets are modelled as separate Types extending the core through ext:type-inheritance; emitters consume the resolved effective Type instead of adding those facets as optional core properties.

sources.excerpt: Owner selects option (a), separate Types extending core via ext:type-inheritance, because optional core Fields would assert extension facets for core-only adopters and erode adopt-only-what-you-need.
The ordering revision explicitly preserves Decision 1 unaltered and lists the live extension-contributed facets to model after the carrier cutover.
The Type prose/schema gaps and RFC-035 exclusions are traced to one cause: the live schema is a flattened union of core and extension facets while metamodel v1.0.0 models core only.

alternatives: Add every live extension facet as an optional Field on the core metamodel Types.
Leave extension facets outside the records and merge them in an emitter overlay.
accepted_cost: Consumers of the metamodel as records must resolve inheritance before they see the effective definition shape.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Flattening facets into core would make extension-owned meaning appear to be core meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Emitters still expose a convenient flattened schema/reference shape after resolving inheritance.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Preserving layer identity without an effective merged view would make the model impractical to consume.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Keep the v1.0 core-only model and tolerate permanent fidelity exclusions.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Existing extension identities and the already-implemented inheritance mechanism are reused rather than replaced.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Inventing a second composition mechanism instead of using inheritance would create needless discontinuity.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A single maximal core would impose facets from extensions on communities that did not adopt them.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: All adopters use the same sanctioned inheritance contract and effective-Type resolution.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Extension autonomy that yields incompatible merge semantics or opaque bags would lose shared coherence.

coding_notes: Ratified owner choice between two explicit architectures. It also supplies the definition-layer extension mechanism requested by #237, but the complete per-entity unknown-field policy remains unresolved in F112.

title: Accept and document inheritance as the sovereign-reader floor
decision_statement: The project accepts that an independent implementation consuming the metamodel records must implement inheritance merging, and requires that raised implementation floor to be recorded as a durable guardrail rather than left implicit.

sources.excerpt: The owner explicitly accepts the higher floor for a from-scratch sovereign reader because inheritance is core to extensibility, and requires the cost to be written into design note 045.
Open, unmerged PR 291 proposes a Tier-0 record carrying the #273 guardrails; it is supporting proposal evidence only and does not establish delivery.

alternatives: Flatten extension facets in the authored core model so a minimal reader need not resolve inheritance.
Accept the cost silently without recording a consumer-facing guardrail.
accepted_cost: A minimal independent definition reader has a larger conformance surface before it can consume the self-hosted metamodel.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Simplify the reader by erasing the semantic distinction between core and extension facets.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The effective merged Type is the practical emitter input, and existing repository machinery already computes it.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: A floor that grows beyond mechanisms necessary for the portability claim would make sovereignty nominal.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: No historical compatibility alternative controls this cost acceptance.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Optimize centrally authored schemas for the easiest consumer at the expense of demonstrating sovereign extension.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Independent readers implement one shared inheritance contract rather than local merge rules.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: If only the reference implementation can realistically meet the floor, the autonomy claim has failed.

coding_notes: PR 291 is intentionally not treated as delivered because mergedAt is null. The owner comment itself ratifies the cost acceptance and documentation obligation.

title: Add contextual FieldAssignment description without semantic override
decision_statement: FieldAssignment gains a per-context description annotation so a reused Field can be explained within a Type, but the annotation is documentation-only: it cannot change Field semantics or AI guidance, and a contradiction is a data error.

sources.excerpt: Owner chooses a per-context description slot rather than permanently genericizing shared Field descriptions, with a normative documentation-only guardrail and Field meaning winning any conflict.
After #242, Decision 2 stands in substance and narrows to description only; its contextual annotation can never override Field semantics.

alternatives: Rewrite shared Field descriptions into context-free generic wording.
Allow Type-local assignments to override a Field's semantics.
Keep contextual explanation only in hand-authored prose outside the model.
accepted_cost: The frozen seed, core structs, emitters, and downstream payload types acquire an additional annotation property and conflict validation rule.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Avoid a schema slot by lowering documentation fidelity or permit contextual prose to mutate shared meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The new annotation directly improves reader-facing contextual expression.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Treating immutable shared semantics as a ban on contextual explanation would make reuse opaque.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserve the frozen seed unchanged and accept the reference-text mismatch.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Existing Field semantics and aiGuidance remain authoritative and unchanged.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Using schema freedom to alter Field meaning through assignments would break semantic continuity.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Either force one generic explanation everywhere or permit unconstrained local reinterpretation.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Shared Field meaning remains coherent while each Type can document its local context.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Either contradictory local descriptions or context-free central wording signals over-rotation.

coding_notes: The balanced coherence/autonomy result is deliberately off-vertex. The slot's later narrowing from description+deprecated to description only is captured separately.

title: Land the contextual annotation in #273 despite seed breakage
decision_statement: Because epic work pauses other consumers and backward compatibility is not a constraint, the FieldAssignment description change remains in #273 instead of being split into a later RFC solely to keep this task smaller.

sources.excerpt: Owner states that core may be broken freely during the paused epic and withdraws the fallback of splitting Decision 2 into its own RFC; the change lands in #273.

alternatives: Defer the description slot to a separate later RFC to minimize #273's immediate blast radius.
accepted_cost: The task reaches the frozen seed, core structs, both emitters, and downstream payload types before unblocking closure.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Optimize task size while knowingly retaining a definition/projection fidelity gap.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The scope remains one narrowly guarded documentation annotation.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Bundling unrelated improvements under compatibility freedom would over-expand the task.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserve seed and downstream shapes temporarily by deferring the breaking addition.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: All paused first-party consumers change together within the epic before ordinary work resumes.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Breaking beyond the coordinated epic boundary would abandon the condition that justified this choice.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Allow the model, emitters, and consumers to remain temporarily divergent across separately scheduled work.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The annotation preserves contextual autonomy within a shared semantic contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Central coordination is justified here by a paused ecosystem, not as a standing ban on independent release cadence.

coding_notes: A project-scoped sequencing decision, not a general license to ignore compatibility. No delivery is claimed while #273 remains open.

title: Initially retain and model the deprecated FieldGroup cluster
decision_statement: Before the epic was reordered, metamodel v1.1.0 was to model the deprecated FieldGroup and assignment-cardinality surface because the live instance carrier and table capability still depended on it, with per-context description and deprecated annotations projected from the model.

sources.excerpt: The initial owner amendment keeps the deprecated surface because its carrier and renderer gates, not backward compatibility, remain active; v1.1.0 was to model it and project deprecation.
The later ordering revision explicitly marks this guidance superseded because #242 now deletes the cluster before #273.

alternatives: Delete the deprecated surface before a conforming replacement carrier and table-rendering path existed.
Ignore the live deprecated surface in closure and preserve it outside the metamodel.
accepted_cost: A deprecated mechanism would temporarily enlarge the self-hosted model and deprecation projector.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Claim model closure while omitting a construct that still carried real table data.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The deprecated cluster was explicitly temporary and tied to a successor path.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Modelling dead compatibility surface after its carrier disappears would preserve syntax without live meaning.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Remove FieldGroup before its live table values had a conforming destination and capability replacement.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The model recorded deprecation and the planned #242/#262 successor rather than normalizing the legacy mechanism.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Retaining the cluster after its replacement lands would convert a gate into inertia.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Let actual first-party data depend on an unmodelled exception while declaring the model complete.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: No external-consumer compatibility claim was used to keep it indefinitely.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: None identified beyond the explicit retirement gate.

coding_notes: Historical decision preserved because the plan requires supersession rather than rewriting. Superseded by E256-F107 later the same day.

title: Model only the live post-carrier definition surface
decision_statement: After #242 was ordered before #273, metamodel v1.1.0 excludes the deleted FieldGroup and assignment-cardinality cluster, narrows FieldAssignment's new annotation to description only, and defers generic deprecation modelling until a live need demonstrates it.

sources.excerpt: The revised order puts #242 first, inverts the earlier guidance, excludes the deleted cluster, narrows the contextual slot to description only, and defers deprecation capability until something needs it.
Epic reconciliation confirms that #273 models only the live post-cutover seed and that the old deprecated-surface advice is superseded.

alternatives: Carry just-deleted deprecated definitions into v1.1.0 for general future usefulness.
Keep the earlier description-plus-deprecated assignment annotation despite no remaining seed site.
accepted_cost: Downstream communities cannot yet express deprecation through this metamodel version and must wait for a demonstrated need and later model revision.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Add speculative capability that no longer describes the live seed and call it closure work.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: The live model remains fully expressible, and a later version can add deprecation when an actual case defines its semantics.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Equating only-currently-used with complete could make the model unable to represent normal lifecycle needs.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Preserve deleted legacy definitions in the next metamodel merely because they were present when analysis began.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The historical decision and the successor carrier remain documented; deletion occurs only after #242 provides the destination.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Deleting a surface before its data and capability have a conforming replacement would repeat the superseded plan's rejected risk.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: The choice is scoped to live model content rather than allocation of central versus local authority.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Later extension Types remain the sanctioned community evolution mechanism.

coding_notes: Supersedes F106. This is definition-layer scope only; the #242 carrier decision itself belongs to family C/E.

title: Verify definition closure at byte level over the full artifact
decision_statement: Definition-layer closure is tested by full byte-level regeneration including annotations and $defs, not by comparing only top-level property key sets; Node and Rust emitters must remain byte-identical.

sources.excerpt: The owner identifies that the key-set reproduction misses annotations and $defs and requires byte-level comparison against a full regenerate before sizing closure.
Epic reconciliation requires full-artifact byte-level regeneration, including annotations and $defs, and byte-identical emitters.

alternatives: Use top-level property-name parity as sufficient evidence of closure.
Allow each emitter to produce semantically similar but byte-different definition artifacts.
accepted_cost: Closure tests become stricter and expose annotation, definition, ordering, and formatting differences that require additional modelling or explicit divergence records.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Declare closure from a lossy comparison that cannot observe parts of the authoritative artifact.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Byte parity applies to deterministic reference artifacts; the fidelity contract may still register justified target limitations.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Treating insignificant formatting as semantic without a deterministic artifact contract would create noise.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Accept silent output drift outside the limited property-key comparison.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Intentional changes remain possible through explicit model revisions and regenerated goldens.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Golden preservation without semantic review would turn tests into accidental authority.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Permit Node and Rust to define subtly different authoritative projections.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Implementations retain independent internals behind the shared byte-level output contract.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Requiring identical internal architecture rather than identical contract output would over-centralize implementation choice.

coding_notes: A stricter F1 application of A12's two-tier closure rule, justified by the discovered blind spot.

title: Settle Field and assignment default semantics
decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether and how Field.defaultValue and FieldAssignment.defaultValue survive, including precedence, application timing, requiredness, allowed-value validity, versioning, and JSON Schema default projection.

sources.excerpt: The open issue lists the independent semantic choices for defaultValue and requires a normative definition or removal.
Epic reconciliation keeps the issue open, routes definition-layer defaultValue decisions into #273, and forbids treating allowlisting as closure.

alternatives: Define Field default semantics and assignment precedence normatively.
Remove one or both default mechanisms from the schema and implementation.
accepted_cost: No cost has been accepted; the unresolved semantics block complete definition-layer closure.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Retention would improve expressive convenience; removal would avoid carrying undefined meaning.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Any resolution must align normative records, projection, and behavior.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Silently generating the existing property would turn schema presence into an unratified semantic decision.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Retention preserves the accepted machine shape; removal simplifies it.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The issue requires explicit version semantics for whichever property survives.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: A shared precedence rule improves coherence; local handling could preserve implementation latitude.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

coding_notes: Open feeder. Generated recommendations are not owner intent; no normative choice is inferred from current schema presence.

title: Choose and define the model's deprecation mechanism
decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether Field.deprecatedAt survives and how it relates to status-based deprecation, read/write semantics, versioning, and JSON Schema deprecated projection; deletion of the old FieldGroup annotations does not settle this Field-level policy.

sources.excerpt: The open issue requires deprecatedAt either to be defined and reconciled with status-based deprecation or removed.
Post-cutover reconciliation still requires #273 to consume #234 decisions for Field.deprecatedAt and deprecation projection even though the old FieldGroup annotation sites are deleted.

alternatives: Retain timestamp deprecation and define its projection and lifecycle semantics.
Converge Field on the substrate status vocabulary.
Remove Field deprecation from this model version.
accepted_cost: No deprecation model cost has yet been chosen; closure cannot merely inherit the schema's existing timestamp shape.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Timestamp, status, and deletion protect different semantic and projection concerns.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Any surviving mechanism must have explicit lifecycle meaning and projection.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Treating a JSON Schema annotation mapping as a substitute for governance semantics would be an integrity failure.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Keeping deprecatedAt preserves current schema shape; convergence or deletion changes it.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The issue requires version semantics for the chosen shape.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Leave Field deprecation inconsistent with the substrate's status-based mechanism.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Entity-specific differences remain possible if made normative and explained.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Uniform syntax without regard to entity lifecycle needs would be false coherence.

coding_notes: The coherence direction reflects the explicit requirement to reconcile or explain the mechanisms, not a choice among timestamp/status/removal. This card remains excluded from bias counts.

title: Make Rust Field parsing uniformly reject unknown properties
decision_statement: The Rust implementation rejects unknown properties consistently for Field, nested FieldTypeConstraints, and ExactTypeRef across create, snapshot, archive, and embedded-bundle paths, while modelling $schema explicitly rather than accepting it as unknown data.

sources.excerpt: Merged PR 778 delivered the RFC-032/RFC-035 adoption and uniform parser behavior.

Owner records that PR 778 implements uniform reject-unknown because the self-hosted Field Type has no extension bag and the schema says additionalProperties false; nested silent-drop paths were also fixed.

alternatives: Preserve unknown top-level Field properties in an untyped extra map.
Reject only at create time while other read paths preserve or silently drop unknown data.
accepted_cost: A newer producer's undeclared definition properties cannot round-trip through this implementation; they fail closed until the model declares an extension path.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Accept or silently drop undeclared keys, yielding path-dependent meaning and lossy round trips.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: $schema is explicitly modelled, and the policy can change with a later schema decision.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Rejecting safely namespaced data after a sanctioned extension mechanism is defined would become rigidity.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Permit future unknown fields but risk deleting them on current read/write paths.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The owner notes a future preserve-unknown spec choice would be a small implementation reversal plus schema change.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: Calling current schema behavior a permanent forward-compatibility policy before normative resolution would overreach.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Different ingestion paths and nested structs would answer unknown-field handling differently.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: Implementation internals remain free so long as every path enforces the declared shape consistently.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Uniform rejection without a sanctioned community extension path would sacrifice bounded evolution.

coding_notes: Distinct from A13's broad Rust adoption card: this records the delivered forward-compatibility behavior surfaced by feeder #237. It is implementation precedent, not normative closure.

title: Ratify a per-entity definition-layer forward-compatibility policy
decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether the normative definition layer adopts reject-unknown or preserve-unknown per entity, how sanctioned extensions interact with that policy beyond inherited extension Types, and whether any escape bag is named meta or properties.

sources.excerpt: The issue requires an explicit policy for every entity, a sanctioned extension point, and resolution or explanation of meta versus properties.
Epic reconciliation says Rust's consistent rejection resolves only the implementation contradiction; #273 still owes definition-layer extension policy and normative schema/engine agreement.

alternatives: Normatively reject all undeclared definition properties and rely on declared inherited extension Types.
Preserve unknown properties, with or without a sanctioned meta/properties bag.
Set different policies per entity with explicit reasons.
accepted_cost: No forward-compatibility cost has been normatively accepted; current Rust rejection remains provisional implementation behavior.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Fail-closed declaration protects known meaning; preservation protects future data and practical round trips.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Whichever policy wins must prevent silent deletion and be stated per entity.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Inferring normative intent from one implementation would collapse evidence hierarchy.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Reject-unknown protects current shape; preserve-unknown allows newer producers to cross older consumers.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: The extension mechanism and version semantics must remain explicit.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: One uniform rule favors coherence; entity-specific or preserved extension space may favor autonomy.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The issue permits justified entity differences but forbids accidental path-dependent behavior.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Uniformity without a usable extension path or autonomy without interoperable rules would each over-rotate.

coding_notes: Kept separate from F111 so delivered engine behavior is not mistaken for ratified spec policy. Instance-layer policy belongs to F2.

title: Resolve Type lineage and provenance disposition
decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether Type.lineage and Type.provenance become modelled definition properties or are removed from the published definition prose because the live fail-closed schema rejects them.

sources.excerpt: The issue reports that published prose declares lineage and provenance while additionalProperties false in the schema rejects them, and requires a per-property disposition.
The #273 scope explicitly requires resolution of #247's definition-layer dispositions, including Type.lineage and Type.provenance.

alternatives: Model lineage and provenance in the self-hosted Type surface and emit them.
Remove the unsupported prose claims and keep the fail-closed schema shape.
accepted_cost: No cost has been selected; prose, model, and schema remain divergent until disposition.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Modelling preserves expressed provenance meaning; removal makes the authoritative machine contract honest and smaller.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Closure requires records, schema, and projection to agree rather than silently selecting one source.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Either current prose or current schema shape must change.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Any retained meaning requires explicit version treatment.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Continue publishing a definition that independent validators reject.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The final model may still expose provenance as a sanctioned optional capability.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Forcing uniform omission without evaluating the provenance use case would be shallow coherence.

coding_notes: Open #247 sub-decision. No schema-is-right default is promoted to owner intent.

title: Resolve FieldAssignment requiredness shape
decision_statement: It remains unresolved whether FieldAssignment.required remains a required boolean property as enforced by the schema or becomes optional as the published pseudo-IDL currently states.

sources.excerpt: The issue identifies requiredness as an optionality mismatch, not a missing documentation line, and requires an explicit disposition.
The #273 outcome includes FieldAssignment requiredness in the definition-layer decisions it must resolve.

alternatives: Require the boolean to be explicitly present in every assignment.
Make the property optional and define an absence default.
accepted_cost: No representation or migration cost has yet been accepted.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Explicit presence reduces ambiguity; optional syntax is more concise but requires default semantics.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Either choice must preserve a determinate requiredness value.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Keeping the schema shape and changing prose differs from changing schema and data.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Let prose and validators continue assigning different meanings to omission.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: The final common rule can still choose concise optional syntax if its default is explicit.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Uniform syntax without an explicit semantic default would not achieve coherence.

coding_notes: Atomic optionality decision split from the other #247 FieldAssignment discrepancies.

title: Remove or sanction FieldAssignment displayHint
decision_statement: It remains unresolved in accepted artifacts whether the schema-rejected FieldAssignment.displayHint is removed from published definition prose or becomes a sanctioned model property; #273 proposes removal but has not yet delivered it.

sources.excerpt: The open issue reports displayHint in prose while the fail-closed schema rejects it and requires an explicit per-property disposition.
The #273 scope proposes removal of the unsanctioned displayHint, but the issue remains open and its coordinator prose is not itself owner ratification or delivery.

alternatives: Remove displayHint from the published definition as unsupported prose.
Model it as a sanctioned presentation annotation with explicit semantics.
accepted_cost: No cost has been chosen; retaining prose preserves an unsupported claim while removal may discard a practical hint without evaluating its use.

integrity_expression.counterfactual: Removal favors a truthful semantic contract; sanctioning may preserve practical presentation expression.
integrity_expression.counterpole_safeguard: Any retained hint must be explicitly presentation-only and projected consistently.
integrity_expression.shadow_signal: Treating issue-scope prose as owner intent would violate the evidence rules.

continuity_evolution.counterfactual: Removal changes published prose; sanctioning changes the machine model.
continuity_evolution.counterpole_safeguard: Either path must be versioned and tested in the full artifact.
continuity_evolution.shadow_signal: None can be established before resolution.

coherence_autonomy.counterfactual: Continue documenting a property that conforming validators reject.
coherence_autonomy.counterpole_safeguard: A sanctioned view-layer annotation remains possible if justified.
coherence_autonomy.shadow_signal: Deleting every locally useful hint merely because it is not yet in the shared schema could over-rotate.

coding_notes: Open proposal kept unresolved. The #273 body is generated/coordinator scope and is not promoted to an accepted decision without owner answer or merge.
